Rik Smits was born on 23 August 1966.
Rik Smits is nicknamed "the Dunking Dutchman."
Rik Smits is a former professional basketball player.
Rik Smits played his entire career with the Indiana Pacers of the NBA.
Rik Smits was drafted by the Indiana Pacers out of Marist College with the second overall pick in the 1988 NBA draft.
Rik Smits reached the NBA Finals in 2000.
Rik Smits was born in Eindhoven.
Rik Smits started playing basketball at age 14 at PSV–Almonte in Eindhoven.
Rik Smits left for the United States in 1984.
Rik Smits played for Marist College for four years.
In 1986, Rik Smits led Marist to the ECAC Metro Conference tournament Championship.
In 1987, Rik Smits led Marist to 20 wins for the first time in its Division I history.
In 1987, Rik Smits helped Marist advance to their first NCAA tournament in school history.
Rik Smits briefly appeared in the 1988 film Coming to America during a scene filmed in 1987 while Marist played against St. John's at Madison Square Garden.
Rik Smits was drafted second overall in the 1988 NBA draft by the Indiana Pacers, becoming the first Marist player to play in the NBA.
Rik Smits' #45 jersey was later retired by Marist.
Rik Smits spent his entire professional career playing for the Indiana Pacers.
With the Pacers, Rik Smits originally backed up Steve Stipanovich.
When Steve Stipanovich suffered a career-ending injury, Rik Smits ended up starting 71 games in his rookie year.
In his rookie year with the Pacers, Rik Smits averaged 11.7 points and 6.1 rebounds per game.
Rik Smits earned All-Rookie First Team honors in his rookie year.
Throughout the Pacers' playoff runs in the mid and late 1990s, Rik Smits was considered the number two player behind Reggie Miller.
In the 1993–94 NBA season, Rik Smits really came into his own as a team leader.
Rik Smits' highest point-per-game average was in 1995–96 when he averaged 18.5 points per game.
On December 10, 1995, Rik Smits scored a career-high 44 points during a 111–104 win over the Los Angeles Clippers.
Rik Smits endeared himself to Pacers fans with outstanding playoff performances.
In Game 4 of the 1995 Eastern Conference Finals, Rik Smits made a buzzer-beating shot to tie the series.
Rik Smits was named to the Eastern Conference All-Star Team in 1998.
In 1998, Rik Smits delivered ten points, seven rebounds and four assists during his All-Star appearance.
Rik Smits included a behind-the-back pass to New Jersey Nets forward Jayson Williams who followed immediately with a slam dunk during the 1998 NBA All-Star Game.
Smits developed nerve damage in his feet from wearing tight shoes as a teenager.
To help recover during the off-season, Rik Smits spent time relaxing at his summer retreat in Walton, New York.
Rik Smits was a regular attendee of The Afton Fair.
Foot problems hobbled Rik Smits for the majority of his career.
Rik Smits retired after the conclusion of the Pacers' 1999–2000 season.
After Indiana was defeated by the Los Angeles Lakers in the NBA Finals 4 games to 2, Rik Smits retired.
Rik Smits has also played for the senior Netherlands national team.
Rik Smits played in the 1986 FIBA World Championship and EuroBasket 1987.
After his retirement, Rik Smits has devoted his time to collecting and racing vintage motocross motorcycles.
On November 30, 2011, Rik Smits was featured in Yahoo! Sports about his formal participation in competitive motocross racing.
In 2008, Rik Smits won the AHRMA Vintage National Premier 500 Intermediate Class riding a BSA 500.
Rik Smits bought a home in the Indianapolis suburb of Zionsville, Indiana, and continued to live there for nearly 20 years.
In 2014, Rik Smits expanded his home in Zionsville to include a regulation-size basketball half-court.
Rik Smits used two barns on the 12.5-acre property to house his motorcycles and cars.
Rik Smits built a dedicated motorcycle track in the rear of the property.
In the summer of 2017, Rik Smits and his girlfriend put the property up for sale after they moved to Arizona.
Rik Smits has two children: a daughter named Jasmine and a son named Derrik.
Jasmine Smits is currently the Player Relations Coordinator for the Indiana Pacers and the Pacers farm team Indiana Mad Ants.
Derrik Smits, listed at 7 feet 2 inches (2.18 m) and 240 pounds (110 kg), played for the Valparaiso University men's basketball team from 2016 to 2019.
In 2019–20, Derrik Smits played his final season of college eligibility at Butler University.
Derrik Smits was forced to redshirt the 2015–16 season due to an injury.

Derrik Smits graduated from Valparaiso in December 2018, taking graduate-level courses in the 2019 spring term to maintain his basketball eligibility; his graduation made him immediately eligible to play at Butler.
